Build it. Test it. Break it. Understand it. Make it better.

The problems I like best are the ones where no single discipline is enough: a sensor board that needs firmware, a controller that needs a sound structure, a test rig that needs both.

It started with building things: a CNC mill, robotic arms, and a lot of electronics. That curiosity grew into PCB design, embedded code, and autonomous machines of every kind, from an indoor patrol drone and a heavy-lift multirotor to a hybrid VTOL aircraft and a Boston Dynamics Spot.

On the hardware side I design boards, including a custom 6-DOF IMU with firmware I wrote myself and a fault-injection PCB for avionics verification. On the software side I work in C and Python with ROS 2, OpenCV, PX4, and ArduPilot.

At Johns Hopkins I'm studying robotics with a focus on automation and control. My interest has moved from building robots to making autonomous systems reliable: hardware-in-the-loop testing, fault injection, telemetry, and debugging the boundary between hardware and software.

Autonomy and aerospace appeal to me because the engineering is unforgiving. A system can't just work in a demo. It has to work repeatedly, under uncertainty, in the real world.

Systems Integration

I learned integration by leading it. As Chief Technical Officer and then President of UAS@UCLA, I oversaw airframe manufacturing, electronics integration, and flight testing across three aircraft, working with the flight controls and propulsion teams to tune PID loops and validate performance in the field.

Aetherguard: Indoor Patrol Drone

UCLA degree capstone, 2026

An autonomous indoor security and patrol drone for warehouses and homes. It combines onboard vision, LiDAR, and real-time decision-making for obstacle avoidance and human recognition.

  • Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano companion computer paired with a Pixhawk 6C flight controller
  • MAVLink, optical flow, and 360° LiDAR for localization in GPS-denied spaces
  • Facial recognition and alert logic in Python and OpenCV

Autonomous eVTOL

UAS@UCLA R&D, 2025. I led this as club President.

A hybrid aircraft that takes off vertically and cruises efficiently on its wing for long-range autonomous missions. 2 m wingspan, 22 minutes of cruise endurance.

  • Quad-plus-dual tilt-motor layout for a smooth hover-to-cruise transition

Testing

My testing experience comes from Joby Aviation, where I coordinated with cross-functional engineers and technicians to design, assemble, and run test rigs for vehicle subsystems, and ran HIL procedures in National Instruments LabVIEW on the ITL to support live flight operations in Dubai.

Avionics Fault-Injection PCB

Joby Aviation, 2025

A custom hardware-in-the-loop board that simulates transient faults and signal interruptions under controlled conditions. I built it under a tight deadline. It was validated on the first iteration and scaled to a bulk order for multiple lab facilities.

  • Designed and assembled in Altium Designer
  • High-frequency relay switching for precise transient faults
  • Impedance-matched differential pairs for ARINC-compliant signal integrity
  • LEMO connectors for rugged, low-noise aircraft-grade interfacing
AltiumHILARINCLabVIEW

Electric Motor Thrust Test Stand

Propulsion characterization

A CAD-designed stand built from aluminum extrusion that measures how a motor and propeller perform across the RPM range. I use the data to choose motor and propeller pairs.

  • Measures thrust, electrical power, and mechanical power
  • Computes motor, ESC, and propeller efficiency
  • Aluminum extrusion frame modeled in CAD
CADPropulsionData analysis

UAS@UCLA and Matter Intelligence
